audits.title: Audit on nursing notes in a psychiatry in-patient setting
audits.standard: MDT-agreed standard for daily progress notes: clear language and information on mental state, medication, meals, physical health, personal care, activities, risks and use of leave

cycle1.result: Accessibility of information scored 1 on average (Likert +3 to -3); language scored 2; personal care information present in 17%.

audits.intervention: Standards and a suggested note format emailed to staff, with follow-up meetings with individual staff and the MDT to resolve difficulties.

cycle2.result: Accessibility 3 on average; language 2; all content items increased; meals, medication and physical health present 100%; personal care 89%.

audits.other_findings: Largest improvement was in personal care information (17% to 89%).
audits.citation: Gunathillaka K, Timbo M, Ginn S. Audit on nursing notes in a psychiatry in-patient setting. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S189-S189. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.511.

audits.title: Inpatient Ward Review Safety Documentation Re-audit
audits.standard: Psychiatry Ward Review Safety Checklist items; 80% completion
audits.setting: Tower Ward, Landermere Centre, Clacton on Sea, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Legal status 93%; resuscitation status 39%; capacity 14%; deteriorating health 64%; physical health concerns 69%; medication review 81%.

cycle2.result: Legal status 88–100%; resuscitation status 42–53%; capacity 67–92%; deteriorating health 100%; physical health 88–92%; medication review 75–88% (across first-week, mid-point and pre-discharge reviews).

audits.other_findings: The electronic checklist was introduced in 2018; all items were over 80% except resuscitation status (40–50%).
audits.citation: Zinchenko O, Meakin Y, Davies L, Bhan - Kotwal S. Inpatient Ward Review Safety Documentation Re-audit. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S181-S181. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.502.

audits.title: Inpatient Ward Review Documentation Audit
audits.standard: 80% completion of ward review documentation questions considered satisfactory
audits.setting: 7 psychiatry wards, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Most questions did not meet the 80% standard; 'Responsible clinician' completed in 23.3%.

audits.intervention: Strategies to improve record keeping, including automation of some fields, junior doctor induction teaching and awareness posters.

cycle2.result: 9 questions satisfactory (at least 80%); 7 above 45%; 17 low; 'Responsible clinician' 99.5% after automation.

audits.other_findings: Effectiveness of non-automated strategies was limited; making fields mandatory or auto-complete worked best.
audits.citation: Nurlu D, Raoof A. Inpatient Ward Review Documentation Audit. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S172-S173. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.454.

audits.title: Psychiatric Emergency Bleep Documentation Enhancement Audit
audits.standard: 90% documentation compliance using a new checklist
audits.setting: West Lothian Psychiatry, district general hospital (Psychiatric 2222 call)

cycle1.result: Psychiatric team documentation 44%; ward nursing documentation 65%; medical ward doctor documentation 39%; appropriate calls 65%.

audits.intervention: Documentation checklist in the electronic records system for completion by the junior doctor, introduced July 2023.

cycle2.result: Documentation 90%; ward nursing documentation 83%; medical ward doctor documentation 57%; appropriate calls 74%.

audits.other_findings: Attending doctors staying longer than 10 minutes rose from 47% to 68%.
audits.citation: Davidova A, Young S, Al Sayegh A, Halford J. Psychiatric Emergency Bleep Documentation Enhancement Audit. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S225-S225. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.553.

audits.title: Audit of Quality and Effectiveness of Clinical Note Entries on a Women’s Low/Medium Secure Forensic Psychiatry Inpatient Unit
audits.standard: CRAMS criteria: 11 points on care plan, risk, activity, mental state and Section 17 leave in daily entries (adopted after CQC Mental Health Act Review)
audits.setting: Women's blended low/medium secure forensic psychiatry inpatient ward

cycle1.result: 814/1540 (52.9%) CRAMS criteria met: care planning 50.5%, risk 70.7%, activity 54.6%, mental state 49.8%, S17 leave 50.3%.

audits.intervention: Findings discussed with the team, an information sheet produced and CRAMS discussed at daily team huddles.

cycle2.period: One year after the initial cycle
cycle2.result: 1120/1540 (71.6%) met: care planning 72.6%, risk 75.0%, activity 70.7%, mental state 70.5%, S17 leave 70.7%.

audits.other_findings: Many entries still did not meet full CRAMS criteria; an electronic template is planned with the new patient record system.
audits.citation: Dillon J. Audit of Quality and Effectiveness of Clinical Note Entries on a Women’s Low/Medium Secure Forensic Psychiatry Inpatient Unit. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S229-S229. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10574.
